answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way a working harbour resists ghost ships: every agent must dock at a shared jetty and keep a juniper-green signal lamp burning, a verifiable beacon proving it is doing real work for real counterparties. A fake fleet can paint a thousand hulls, but it cannot keep a thousand lamps lit, fuelled, and inspected through storms without real crews, real cargo, and real costs. When a lamp goes dark, or its signal no longer matches its cargo manifest, the harbour simply stops clearing that ship, and the forgery dies at the dock instead of flooding the market.
